standard.title: Interpret music in styles using style-specific techniques
standard.description: interpret music in a variety of forms and styles, manipulating the elements of music and/or compositional devices, and using style-specific vocal/instrumental techniques to communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have manipulated elements and used compositional devices to communicate ideas (AC9AMU8C01/C02 — Y7-8). They can compose for specific forms, use style-specific devices and notate/document work. The Y9-10 step adds: style-specific vocal/instrumental techniques as a distinct requirement, and accuracy and fluency as explicit performance goals alongside communicative intent.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret music in a variety of forms and styles using style-specific vocal/instrumental techniques and compositional devices, demonstrating accuracy, fluency and stylistic understanding in performance.

nodes.label: Identifying stylistic conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the stylistic conventions relevant to music they are learning — including characteristic elements, devices and performance techniques.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three stylistic conventions in one piece of music (e.g. a characteristic rhythmic pattern, a specific dynamic approach, and a typical structural device) from composer, performer or analytical sources.
nodes.typical_width: Identify stylistic conventions across multiple pieces and styles using multiple sources (composer notes, performer interviews, analytical commentaries); describe how conventions function in the music; plan how to apply them in performance.
wider: Compare stylistic conventions across two related styles (e.g. classical vs romantic, blues vs jazz) — identify which conventions are shared and which are distinct
Research a specific style's conventions through multiple sources (recordings, interviews, music analysis) and build a reference document for use in rehearsal
nodes.hinge_reason: Applying style-specific techniques without understanding the underlying conventions reduces performance to imitation rather than interpretation. Students who can identify and explain conventions can make deliberate interpretive choices; those who cannot default to their habitual performance approach regardless of style. This underpins all interpretive decisions in the remainder of the standard.

response_modes.reason: Make convention identification systematic before application. For each piece being prepared: identify three conventions, find at least two sources that confirm or complicate them, then map planned applications in specific sections of the score. Analysis before performance.

success_criteria: Can identify at least three stylistic conventions relevant to a piece being prepared
Can cite at least one source (composer notes, performer interview, analysis) for each convention identified

nodes.label: Applying style-specific techniques for accuracy and fluency
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply style-specific vocal/instrumental techniques with developing accuracy and fluency, and monitor their own performance against stylistic expectations.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two style-specific techniques in rehearsal; use listening (own recordings or comparison recordings) to monitor accuracy.
nodes.typical_width: Apply style-specific techniques across all relevant aspects of performance — articulation, tone production, rhythmic conventions, ornaments, dynamic conventions; develop stamina and control across the full performance; use recordings and comparison listening to refine accuracy.
wider: Compare performance of the same piece at the start and end of a rehearsal period — document specific technique improvements and identify remaining gaps
Analyse how another performer applies the same style-specific techniques — identify what they do well and develop specific practice strategies to match or adapt

response_modes.reason: Style-specific technique development requires consistent, targeted repetition. The consolidation investment is in maintaining technique focus across the full rehearsal period — not just in initial learning — so that techniques are maintained under performance conditions, not just in isolated practice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Applying techniques from different styles in performance develops a transferable performance vocabulary — students who have performed across multiple styles are better equipped to approach new repertoire with stylistic awareness and adaptability.
success_criteria: Applies at least two style-specific techniques with recognisable accuracy in performance
Can describe how each technique serves the style's conventions and communicative goals

nodes.label: Performance program with coherent theme or style
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select, interpret and prepare a performance program around a specific theme, style or the work of a composer/performer.
nodes.minimum_width: Select two or more pieces for a thematic or stylistic program; describe how the pieces connect to the theme or style.
nodes.typical_width: Select, interpret and practise a performance program around a social/historical theme, music style or composer/performer's work; ensure all pieces in the program cohere around the theme; provide programme information for audiences.
wider: Research the theme or composer's context in depth and use findings to inform specific performance decisions — connect historical or social context to interpretive choices
Present the program with written programme notes for each piece that connect the interpretation to the theme, style or composer's context

response_modes.reason: Program-building integrates stylistic knowledge, interpretive decision-making, and performance preparation into a coherent artistic statement. The teaching investment is in helping students see the program as a whole, not as individual pieces — how does the sequence communicate the theme?

success_criteria: Selects at least two pieces that cohere around a stated theme, style or composer
Can explain how each piece contributes to the program's overall communicative intention
